query: For magnetic high-entropy alloys, what single intervention could increase the coercive field? State one testable hypothesis that specifies the intervention, the mechanism expected to alter coercivity, the predicted outcome relative to a matched baseline, the conditions under which the effect should hold, the prior evidence supporting the hypothesis, and an experiment with a clear result that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Substitution of elements with high magnetic moments in magnetic high-entropy alloys will increase the coercive field by modifying magnetic anisotropy and exchange interactions.
generation.intervention: substitution of 5 at.% of Fe with Co in the alloy composition
generation.mechanism: modification of magnetic anisotropy and exchange interactions due to the substitution of elements with high magnetic moments
generation.predicted_outcome: increase in coercive field by 20% relative to a matched baseline of the unmodified alloy
generation.baseline: coercive field of the unmodified alloy (10 kOe)
generation.boundary: coercive field increase below 5% is not significant
generation.uncertainty: the actual increase in coercive field may vary depending on the specific alloy composition and processing conditions

falsification_experiment.design: prepare two sets of magnetic high-entropy alloy samples, one with the substitution of 5 at.% of Fe with Co and one without, and measure their coercive fields at room temperature and standard atmospheric pressure
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: if the coercive field of the modified alloy is not at least 15% higher than that of the unmodified alloy, the hypothesis is falsified
